proposed_widenings.name: spellcasting_framework
proposed_widenings.justification: Wizard Spellcasting is a passive infrastructure feature — it does not activate for a use-count; it establishes the spell slot pool, spellbook, and prepared list that all subsequent casting draws on. The existing ClassFeatureMechanics family 'activation' requires activationCost + resource (use_count) + resetCadence + effect, which cannot represent 'grants a multi-tier slot pool, a stored-spell object, and a dynamic prepared list'. A new family is required.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Spell Slots. The Wizard Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

proposed_widenings.name: spell_slot_pool
proposed_widenings.justification: Spell slots are not a scalar use_count — they are a level-indexed pool (e.g. 2 × L1 slots at wizard L1, growing to multiple levels and counts per the features table). UseCountResource with UseCountCap cannot represent this; it only tracks a single integer cap.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest. [implicit: slots are partitioned by spell level, each independently consumed]

proposed_widenings.name: grant_spell_access
proposed_widenings.justification: ClassFeatureEffect is currently GrantExtraActionEffect | HealHpEffect. The grant_spell_access atom exists in the v4 taxonomy but has no surface variant in ClassFeatureEffect. Wizard Spellcasting's core function is granting access to a spell list (cantrips known + spells in spellbook + prepared list), which requires this variant.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Cantrips. You know three Wizard cantrips of your choice. [...] The book contains the level 1+ spells you know. It starts with six level 1 Wizard spells of your choice.

proposed_widenings.name: spellbook_object
proposed_widenings.justification: The spellbook is a physical Tiny object (v4 attachment kind 'object') that acts as a stored-spell repository with rules for adding spells and copying. No surface shape for 'object that holds a mutable stored-spell list' exists in the current Attachment or effect vocabulary. The spellbook also doubles as a valid spellcasting focus, adding a dual-role dimension not covered by any existing surface type.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Your wizardly apprenticeship culminated in the creation of a unique book: your spellbook. It is a Tiny object [...] The book contains the level 1+ spells you know.

notes: No honest coercion is possible. The 'activation' family requires a discrete activation event with a use-count and a terminal effect. Wizard Spellcasting has no activation event — it is always-on infrastructure. Attempting to encode it as activation would require fabricating a 'free' activation cost and a nonsensical use_count cap, producing a trace that misrepresents the feature as an activated ability. The multi-tier spell slot pool (level-indexed) is structurally distinct from use_count (scalar). The prepared-list mechanic (subset of spellbook, changeable on Long Rest) has no surface analog. The spellbook-as-spellcasting-focus dual role is also unrepresented.
